Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-20
Time: 15:00 - 15:42 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sarah Lee (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Gomez (Redwood CSM), Dana Rivera (Orion CTO), Amit Shah (Orion ML Ops), Priya Nair (Orion DevOps), Leo Park (Orion Security)

Summary:
Quick onboarding kickoff to align pilot goals, infrastructure requirements (VPC/on-prem options), security/compliance checks, timeline for a 4-week pilot and next steps to get a test environment running.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sarah Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sarah from Redwood, AE on the account. Uh, we'll run through the kickoff agenda, quick intros, pilot goals, infra, security, and then wrap with next steps. Marcus will do a short SE overview.
[00:12] Dana Rivera: Hi all, Dana here, CTO at Orion. Excited to get started.
[00:16] Amit Shah: Amit - Head of ML Ops. We'll be leading the techPilot on our side.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Priya, DevOps. I'll be doing VPC stuff.
[00:24] Leo Park: Leo, Security. I'll be validating SOC2/KMS requirements.
[00:30] Marcus Patel: Great, thanks. I'll jump into the SE bits. We're planning a 4-week pilot to validate latency and throughput for your internal chat/triage use case, and to test private deployment options.
[00:40] Marcus Patel: First question for team - are you planning Hosted API or Private (VPC/on-prem)? Or a mix?
[00:47] Amit Shah: We're leaning private VPC to start, because of PHI concerns in a few workflows. We might evaluate hosted for less-sensitive stuff later.
[00:55] Marcus Patel: Makes sense. For VPC we do a private control plane model where the data path is within your VPC, and we support peering or private link, and optional on-prem packages if needed.
[01:10] Priya Nair: Can you send us the sample peering setup or terraform? Also, does Redwood support cross-account peering for multi-region?
[01:18] Marcus Patel: Yep - we'll share terraform snippets. Cross-region peering is supported, though note there are latency implications; we'll surface region routing suggestions in the docs.
[01:30] Leo Park: Security checklist - we need SOC 2 report, encryption at rest and in transit, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, RBAC and SSO (SAML). Also data retention and deletion policies.
[01:45] Elena Gomez: We'll attach SOC2 and the security whitepaper after the call. We support customer-managed KMS keys, audit logs are available and we can map roles for RBAC. SAML SSO is supported for console access.
[01:58] Dana Rivera: For success criteria, we'll measure: 1) 99th percentile latency under typical load, 2) per-token cost targets, and 3) ability to run in our VPC with proper audit logs.
[02:10] Sarah Lee: Good, that aligns with our pilot checklist. Marcus, quick on benchmarks - what should they expect for latency on a standard LLM?
[02:18] Marcus Patel: For a 2k token sequence on a quantized 8-bit model on a dedicated GPU pool, typical p99 is under 700ms in our tests; but in VPC setups you'll see a little extra egress/peering overhead. We will run an initial benchmark with your sample prompts.
[02:34] Amit Shah: Are you doing automatic model fallbacks if capacity is constrained? We had some outages with another provider.
[02:40] Marcus Patel: Yes, smart routing is part of the platform - you can configure fallbacks to compatible model variants or lower-cost tiers. For the pilot we can show a canary rollout and fallback policy.
[02:52] Priya Nair: About data retention - can we set per-route retention and automatic purge?
[02:58] Elena Gomez: Yes, per-route retention is configurable; we'll send the retention config examples.
[03:06] Leo Park: Also need proof of encryption keys managed on our side. KMS integration details?
[03:12] Marcus Patel: Customer-managed KMS is supported; we provide guidance for AWS KMS and HSM integrations. For on-prem, we have an HSM integration guide.
[03:22] Dana Rivera: Any major blockers you foresee on our side for a 4-week pilot?
[03:27] Marcus Patel: Main items: VPC peering setup, sample dataset and prompts for benchmarks, and a small traffic generator to simulate expected QPS. If you can provide those in week one we can run meaningful numbers in week two.
[03:40] Amit Shah: We'll provide sample prompts and a representative dataset — non-PHI subset initially.
[03:45] Sarah Lee: Timeline suggestion: week 1 - infra and access, week 2 - baseline benchmarks, week 3 - integrations and telemetry, week 4 - evaluation and handoff.
[03:56] Priya Nair: Sounds good. For infra, do you need any specific IAM roles?
[04:00] Marcus Patel: Just a set of least-privilege roles for provisioning the peering and S3 buckets for model artifacts if you host variants. We'll send an IAM policy example.
[04:10] Leo Park: Compliance question - will logs contain PII? We need to ensure redaction or tokenization options.
[04:16] Elena Gomez: We have options for automatic redaction and a configurable filter pipeline before logs are persisted. We'll include those in the security docs.
[04:26] Dana Rivera: On pricing - we might need Dedicated reserved capacity if we scale. Can you share ballpark committed pricing and the delta vs hosted?
[04:34] Sarah Lee: Yes - I'll share a pricing sheet after the call. Dedicated typically provides a lower per-token cost at commit; we'll include burst policies and SLA terms.
[04:44] Amit Shah: Any integration examples for our stack? We're on AWS with Kubernetes, and use Airflow for orchestration.
[04:51] Marcus Patel: We have Kubernetes operator examples, Airflow DAG snippets, and a Terraform module for VPC peering. We'll share links.
[04:58] Priya Nair: What about monitoring and observability? We need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards forwarded to our Datadog.
[05:06] Marcus Patel: The Redwood Console provides per-route metrics and you can forward traces and metrics to Datadog via our exporter. We'll enable a demo dashboard during the pilot.
[05:18] Leo Park: Also, audit trail for model rollouts—need to know who changed which model and when.
[05:24] Elena Gomez: Rollouts are auditable; we keep change history and can export to your SIEM.
[05:30] Dana Rivera: Ok let's capture the immediate next steps, and owners.
[05:34] Sarah Lee: Quick recap: Marcus will send implementation checklist, terraform snippets, IAM policy; Elena will set up pilot invites and Slack channel; Sarah will send pricing sheet and SOC2 docs; Orion team will provide sample prompts, confirm stakeholders and stand up test VPC.
[05:50] Amit Shah: One more thing - latency SLOs: can we set alerting for degradation?
[05:56] Marcus Patel: Absolutely, we can set SLOs and tie alerts to a webhook or PagerDuty.
[06:02] Priya Nair: Great.
[06:04] Sarah Lee: Any final questions?
[06:06] Dana Rivera: No, that's all for now. Looking forward.
[06:09] Sarah Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and the calendar invites.

[End of call]
